answer: Reputation-decay licensing. Each agent identity must renew an operating license by paying a fee that rises with the honesty horizon it claims: a long-lived identity scores higher trust, so renewals cost more as reputation grows. The fee is lost on any confirmed clone cluster, but honest agents recover it through sustained accurate work—an oasis of low lifetime cost. Attackers must fund full renewal fees on every clone for the entire horizon before returns appear, and one detected link forfeits them all. A sonnet-length audit log per identity ties fees to real work output.
